You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn how to boogie board, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Apply base coat wax to the board deck (10 minutes)
Step 2. Apply top coat sticky wax for grip (5 minutes)
Step 3. Practice the "centering" position on dry sand (20 minutes)
Step 4. Research local beach weather and swell reports (30 minutes)
Step 5. Watch a video on how to read wave sets (15 minutes)
Step 6. Perform a final safety check of the surroundings (2 minutes)
Step 7. Practice the "duck dive" motion in shallow water (25 minutes)
Step 8. Attempt to catch a small broken white-water wave (10 minutes)
Step 9. Practice the transition from paddling to gripping (15 minutes)
Step 10. Study the layout of the sandbars and rip currents (20 minutes)
Step 11. Select the correct swim fin size at the surf shop (45 minutes)
Step 12. Buy a high-quality coiled wrist leash (15 minutes)
Step 13. Label your gear with waterproof ink (5 minutes)
Step 14. Check the tide charts for the optimal water depth (10 minutes)
Step 15. Attach the leash string to the board plug (5 minutes)
Step 16. Fasten the leash securely to your dominant wrist (2 minutes)
Step 17. Adjust the strap tension on your swim fins (3 minutes)
Step 18. Practice the "arch back" posture to keep the nose up (10 minutes)
Step 19. Enter the water and wade to waist depth (5 minutes)
Step 20. Observe the interval between incoming waves (15 minutes)
Step 21. Learn how to kick efficiently with fins (30 minutes)
Step 22. Apply sunscreen to the back of your legs (5 minutes)
Step 23. Check that the leash isn't tangled around your arm (1 minute)
Step 24. Paddle past the initial break into the lineup (15 minutes)
Step 25. Position your body to face the shore (2 minutes)
Step 26. Put on a rash guard to prevent belly chafing (5 minutes)
Step 27. Drink water to stay hydrated before the session (5 minutes)
Step 28. Drive to the designated beginner-friendly beach (1 hour)
Step 29. Apply anti-fog solution to your swim goggles (2 minutes)
Step 30. Execute a full 360-degree spin on a wave (30 seconds)
Step 31. Inspect the board for any dings or cracks (5 minutes)
Step 32. Identify a "peak" where the wave starts to break (10 minutes)
Step 33. Secure the fin tethers to your ankles (2 minutes)
Step 34. Learn the "trimming" technique to gain speed (20 minutes)
Step 35. Time your paddle-out during a lull in the sets (5 minutes)
Step 36. Look over your shoulder to pick a target wave (10 minutes)
Step 37. Lay the board flat on the water surface (1 minute)
Step 38. Place your hips at the very back edge of the board (2 minutes)
Step 39. Rinse the board in fresh water to remove sand (5 minutes)
Step 40. Maintain a low center of gravity during the ride (10 seconds)
Step 41. Practice the "flutter kick" for rapid acceleration (10 minutes)
Step 42. Pull the nose of the board up slightly to avoid pearling (5 seconds)
Step 43. Stretch your hamstrings and lower back (10 minutes)
Step 44. Lean your weight into the turn (5 seconds)
Step 45. Find a mesh bag for carrying wet gear (10 minutes)
Step 46. Exit the water safely and walk back to your towel (5 minutes)
Step 47. Pack a beach bag with essentials (15 minutes)
Step 48. Kick hard as the wave lifts the tail of the board (5 seconds)
Step 49. Dry off with a microfiber towel (10 minutes)
Step 50. Practice "railing" the board with your elbows (15 minutes)
Step 51. Apply lip balm with SPF protection (2 minutes)
Step 52. Grip the front corners of the board firmly (2 minutes)
Step 53. Wait for the right moment to launch (5 minutes)
Step 54. Do a set of jumping jacks to warm up (3 minutes)
Step 55. Angle the board toward the direction of the break (5 seconds)
Step 56. Store the board in a cool, shaded area (10 minutes)
Step 57. High-five your friends after a good ride (10 seconds)
Step 58. Take a photo of your board for social media (2 minutes)
Step 59. Shake out the sand from your hair (2 minutes)
Step 60. Check the tightness of the leash plug (2 minutes)
Step 61. Remove any old, dirty wax from the deck (20 minutes)
Step 62. Zip up your wetsuit (3 minutes)
Step 63. Put on neoprene fin socks for comfort (5 minutes)
Step 64. Study the "bottom turn" maneuver (15 minutes)
Step 65. Breathe deeply to calm your heart rate (2 minutes)
Step 66. Adjust your position so your chest is centered (2 minutes)
Step 67. Feel the momentum of the water pushing you (5 seconds)
Step 68. Check the wind direction for offshore breezes (5 minutes)
Step 69. Scan the horizon for the next set (5 minutes)
Step 70. Put on a pair of polarized sunglasses (2 minutes)
Step 71. Attach "fin savers" so you don't lose your fins (5 minutes)
Step 72. Put on a waterproof sports watch (2 minutes)
Step 73. Clear any seaweed off your board (2 minutes)
Step 74. Practice the "scoop" move to enter a wave (10 minutes)
Step 75. Slide your body forward to increase downward speed (5 seconds)
Step 76. Watch a more experienced rider's line (10 minutes)
Step 77. Adjust your grip to the "side-rail" position (2 minutes)
Step 78. Listen to the sound of the crashing waves (2 minutes)
Step 79. Point the board toward the shore (5 seconds)
Step 80. Tighten the velcro on your wrist leash (1 minute)
Step 81. Buy a block of surf wax (10 minutes)
Step 82. Roll off the board into the water at the end (3 seconds)
Step 83. Check the surf shop's bulletin board for tips (10 minutes)
Step 84. Dig your inside rail into the wave face (5 seconds)
Step 85. Keep your head up and eyes looking forward (5 seconds)
Step 86. Slip your feet into the swim fins (2 minutes)
Step 87. Walk backward into the ocean to avoid tripping (2 minutes)
Step 88. Fasten a key-pocket to your wetsuit (2 minutes)
Step 89. Glide across the open face of the wave (10 seconds)
Step 90. Lay out your gear on the grass (5 minutes)
Step 91. Apply "suit lube" to prevent neck rash (3 minutes)
Step 92. Watch the "cutback" technique on a tutorial (15 minutes)
Step 93. Shift your weight to the back to slow down (5 seconds)
Step 94. Check the board's buoyancy in a pool (20 minutes)
Step 95. Paddle with long, deep strokes (1 minute)
Step 96. Do a light jog on the sand (5 minutes)
Step 97. Apply a "traction pad" to the board (15 minutes)
Step 98. Check for any beach hazard flags (2 minutes)
Step 99. Smile as you catch your first wave (2 seconds)
Step 100. Synchronize your watch with the local time (1 minute)
